title: Asset-card FIX doctrine test is a tautology — asserts on a button that is never disabled
evidence:
test_economy.gd:1030-1033:
	var fix_card: Control = _street._make_asset_card(_street._state["assets"][0])
	var fix_btn: Button = fix_card.get_child(0).get_child(2)
	check(not fix_btn.disabled, "asset-card FIX enabled for a free repair at negative balance")
	fix_card.free()

street.gd:371-376 (_make_asset_card's button — the one the test reads):
	var open := Button.new()
	open.text = "🔧 FIX" if asset["damaged"] else "👀 OPEN"
	open.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(170, 130)
	open.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 26)
	open.pressed.connect(_show_asset_popup.bind(asset["id"]))
	row.add_child(open)
(no `.disabled =` assignment anywhere in _make_asset_card)

street.gd:782 (the actual doctrine fix, in _show_asset_popup — a different button the test never builds):
		fix.disabled = fix_cost > 0 and _state["balance"] < fix_cost
detail: The test reads _make_asset_card's OPEN/FIX button, which has no balance gate, so `not fix_btn.disabled` is vacuously true. The real fix lives in _show_asset_popup (a _make_big_button the test never opens), so the AC5/PR-body claim that free-FIX-from-debt is pinned is unenforced.
recommended_fix: Drive the probe through _show_asset_popup (open the popup, read its FIX button's .disabled) instead of _make_asset_card, so the fix_cost>0/balance gate is actually exercised at negative balance.
